page: Microsoft Azure FX96-24mds_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual machine instance configured with 24 dedicated vCPUs on an x86_64 Intel processor architecture. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, the configuration is characterized by a high memory-to-core allocation, offering 1832.0 GB of system RAM, which translates to roughly 76.33 GB of memory per core. Accelerated hardware coprocessors are absent, with zero GPUs included.

For local disk operations, the instance features 5669 GB of NVMe SSD direct-attached storage alongside support for Premium Storage. Architecturally, constraining the active processing allocation to 24 vCPUs out of a larger host footprint allows workloads to capitalize on a massive memory pool and high-speed local disk capacity without incurring the software licensing overhead typically associated with higher core counts.

This hardware balance is structured specifically for memory-heavy and I/O-intensive enterprise workloads. Key target applications include large-scale in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), relational databases with per-core licensing constraints, extensive data caching systems, and high-throughput data transformation pipelines requiring fast local scratch storage.
